edits.html:
Screening USPSTF (US Preventive Services Task Force) recommends screening every sexually active woman under 25 for chlamydia and gonorrhea · the screening test is NAAT (nucleic acid amplification testing) for both organisms, even with no discharge and a normal exam · most infections are silent, and treating them prevents PID (pelvic inflammatory disease) and its sequelae. How NBME framed it: each decoy option had a planted cue, such as the mother's breast cancer at 40, and the key named the test in full.
Pairs with Part II Cervical Screening: the Age-21 Floor: is she 21 or older, or is she due only for chlamydia and gonorrhea screening?

edits.html:
True-fact-wrong-slotPap smear — cervical cytology starts at 21 whatever the sexual history, so a sexually active 16-year-old gets chlamydia and gonorrhea screening instead
Salient decoyMammography — the mother's breast cancer at 40 is a planted cue; routine mammography starts at 40, not in adolescence
Unchecked attributeFasting serum glucose — a body mass index of 25 alone does not meet the adolescent diabetes screening bar, which needs overweight plus risk factors such as insulin resistance
Salient decoyHemoglobin concentration — irregular menses are a planted cue; the US Preventive Services Task Force does not recommend routine screening for iron deficiency anemia
edits.note: Q27: one trapline per original distractor (Pap, mammography, glucose, hemoglobin)
